situation.text: PST says Russian mapping of Norwegian infrastructure, military targets and arms makers has grown through 2026, and warns that Russia may use criminals and other proxies for missions in Norway, as in the foiled Danish murder plot. The government wants to spend about NOK 21 bn on new NASAMS missiles to protect air bases, critical infrastructure and allied reception areas.

Finland's coast guard confirms that Ukrainian drones hit the Russian cargo ship Sparta II, which drifted burning into Finnish waters; a Russian helicopter flew over 4 km into Finnish airspace during the rescue. Finland's prime minister says the war is spreading to Finland's neighbourhood. Denmark is expelling Russia's military attaché over a Russian-planned murder plot near Copenhagen.

A Russian drone hit an apartment block in Dymer near Kyiv on 22 November, killing at least ten people. President Zelensky says Russia is trying to cut the Odesa and Dnipro regions off from power by destroying grids and transmission lines. The UK and Ukraine signed deals to build Ukrainian-designed strike drones in Britain with UK money.

Polish investigators now say all three objects that fell in Poland on 20 November were Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles made in late 2026, and Poland is calling for stronger NATO air defence. Drones were reported over Russia's Baltic Fleet base at Baltiysk in Kaliningrad on 21 November. Canada joined the NATO Innovation Fund, which now has more than EUR 1.1 bn.

news.title: PST: Russia is mapping Norwegian arms makers and recruiting proxies
news.summary: PST says Russian mapping of Norwegian infrastructure, military targets and weapons producers has increased through 2026. Such mapping can be preparation for sabotage. PST also warns of more use of proxies, such as criminals, and says Norwegian citizens and Ukrainian refugees have been approached to carry out tasks in Norway. The warning follows Denmark's finding that Russia planned a murder near Copenhagen.

news.title: FMA keeps the Navy vessel race national but will not demand Norwegian hulls
news.summary: FMA says the 28 standardised vessels will be bought through a national competition, split into two contracts so more Norwegian yards can meet the financial requirements. Yards can also team up or use a supporting company to meet them. Hulls may be built in Norway, but FMA will not require it. Prime Minister Støre told DN that most value for Norwegian industry lies in what goes on board, and Parliament's defence committee wants the ships built in Norway.

news.title: Norway plans NOK 21 bn buy of NASAMS missiles
news.summary: The government's revised 2026 defence budget proposes buying AIM-9X, AMRAAM 120C and AMRAAM-ER missiles for NASAMS, with a cost frame (P85) of NOK 21.3 bn. The missiles will protect the fighter base at Ørland, Evenes, critical infrastructure, allied reception areas and Army units against drones, aircraft and helicopters. The buy replaces old missiles and those donated to Ukraine, and builds larger stocks. NordicDefenceWatch reports that Kongsberg may soon produce AMRAAM missiles in Norway.

news.title: Report: labour shortage pushes Norwegian defence growth abroad
news.summary: A Menon Economics report finds that some larger Norwegian defence companies are already putting new capacity abroad because the home labour market is exhausted. Kongsberg companies account for about 45% of the Norwegian defence industry's turnover. Access to skilled staff, not orders, is becoming the bottleneck.

news.title: Norway's next battlegroup in Lithuania takes attack drones
news.summary: Contingent 21 deploys to NATO's battlegroup in Lithuania in January with drones for reconnaissance, observation and attack. The force commander says this follows NATO's push and the growing drone community in Norway. Drones are moving from trials into regular Norwegian units.

news.title: Kongsberg joins Ukraine's Brave Prime programme
news.summary: Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace has signed a memorandum with Brave1 and joined Brave Prime, after Airbus and Saab. Kongsberg will test its systems in Ukraine under Test in Ukraine. The two sides will also look for Ukrainian companies whose technology and components can be built into Kongsberg's systems, and for joint research areas. The deal was signed in Kyiv by Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace Ukraine.

news.title: Teleplan Globe links Ukraine's Raybird drone into its FACNAV battle system
news.summary: Norwegian Teleplan Globe and Ukrainian drone maker Skyeton have integrated the ACS-3 Raybird long-endurance drone into the FACNAV battle management system. Operators get live video from the Raybird in the same view as other drones, ground cameras and satellites, which cuts the time from detection to strike. When the work is done, operators will be able to plan missions and control the drone and its payload from FACNAV.

news.title: Forsvaret cancels the big Valiant Defender exercise planned for 2027
news.summary: The Chief of Defence has dropped Valiant Defender, a large allied exercise planned for March 2027, possibly in Finnmark and Indre Troms, citing changed strategic priorities. Resources go instead to Heimdall in February, a trial of autonomous systems in Arctic conditions, and NATO's Formidable Shield missile exercise at Andøya in April. Joint Viking will be held in Indre Troms in March with about 4,000 troops, and Cold Response 2028 is planned to be larger. Heimdall is the 2027 test window to watch for autonomy startups.

news.title: Finland confirms Ukrainian drones hit Sparta II; Russian helicopter enters Finnish airspace
news.summary: Finland's coast guard confirms that two Ukrainian drones hit the sanctioned Russian cargo ship Sparta II, which then drifted burning into Finnish waters. The crew was evacuated by another Russian vessel. A Russian helicopter flew more than 4 km into Finnish airspace, linked to the rescue. Prime Minister Orpo said the war is spreading to Finland's neighbourhood.

news.title: Drones hit a Russian cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland
news.summary: The Russian cargo ship Sparta II, bound for Kaliningrad, caught fire in the Gulf of Finland on 21 November; the Leningrad region governor says two drones hit it. Overnight, NATO jets were scrambled over Estonia after drone warnings, and Finland restricted flights and shipping in the eastern gulf. No violation of Estonian or Finnish airspace is confirmed.

news.title: Denmark expels Russia's military attaché over a murder plot
news.summary: Denmark's security service PET says Russian intelligence planned the attempted murder of a Ukrainian-American citizen that was stopped north of Copenhagen in September. The killing was to be carried out by people linked to the banned gang Loyal to Familia. Two people are charged, and the attaché must leave within seven days.

news.title: Latvian Rannon readies mini anti-drone rockets for Ukraine
news.summary: Rannon is finishing 1.2 kg unguided air-to-air rockets that can be fitted to fixed-wing drones or quadcopters, typically 4 to 12 per carrier. They have a proximity fuse and use a ballistic computer and AI target recognition. The company is preparing tests in Ukraine.

news.title: Finland orders EUR 462 m of explosives from Nammo and Componenta
news.summary: The purchases are part of Finland's ammunition production programme. The defence ministry says they will create almost 1,200 person-years of work in Finland. Nammo is jointly owned by Norway and Finland.

news.title: Nordic Air Defence tests its K200 interceptor in Ukraine
news.summary: Swedish startup Nordic Air Defence will hand its new K200 interceptor drones to Ukrainian forces for testing and has opened an office in Ukraine. The company says the K200 can catch jet-powered drones such as the Geran-4. It plans to make 1,000 interceptors a month by March 2027, with development and assembly in Sweden.

news.title: Vidhance to track drones for Valkyr's Hildr system
news.summary: Swedish video software firm Vidhance and Valkyr Defense Systems have signed an agreement for drone tracking in the Hildr system. A prototype will be shown to FMV, Sweden's procurement agency, in March 2027.

news.title: Systematic, Netcompany and Terma compete for Danish warfare software
news.summary: Denmark is close to choosing a supplier for its future military software. Systematic, Netcompany and Terma are competing for a first contract worth several hundred million Danish kroner. All three bidders are Danish.

news.title: Russian drone strike in Dymer kills ten as grid attacks continue
news.summary: A Russian drone hit a five-storey apartment building in Dymer, Kyiv region, overnight on 22 November; the death toll has risen to ten. President Zelensky says Russia is trying to cut the Odesa and Dnipro regions off from power by destroying grids and transmission lines, causing large outages.

news.title: UK and Ukraine agree to build Ukrainian strike drones in Britain
news.summary: The UK and Ukrainian defence ministers signed agreements in Kyiv for UK-funded production of Ukrainian middle-strike and deep-strike drones in Britain. Ukraine can set up production facilities in the UK. The deals follow a further GBP 500 m of UK aid, of which GBP 260 m is for drones and GBP 240 m for air defence. The model of Ukrainian designs built in partner countries keeps spreading.

news.title: Russian strike on Kryvyi Rih injures 73
news.summary: Ballistic missiles and drones hit Kryvyi Rih on the evening of 20 November and overnight. Two people were killed and 73 injured, including nine children. About 26 apartment buildings, a hospital and schools were damaged.

news.title: EU approves another EUR 1 bn for Ukrainian weapons
news.summary: The EU Council approved EUR 1 bn from the European Peace Facility for joint procurement of drones, air defence, ammunition, electronic warfare, radars and explosives for delivery by the end of 2027. It is part of a EUR 6.6 bn political decision on EPF support to Ukraine.

news.title: SkyFall and Auterion to build a drone factory in Germany
news.summary: Ukrainian SkyFall and Auterion are forming the joint venture SkyFall x Auterion to make drones in Germany under the Build with Ukraine programme. They have already supplied over 50,000 Shrike strike drones to Ukraine. The plant starts with Shrike FPV drones and later adds interceptors and medium- and long-range strike drones, possibly for the Bundeswehr too.

news.title: Russian ballistic missiles hit Kyiv bridges and kill three
news.summary: Russia attacked Kyiv with ballistic missiles overnight into 20 November. Three people were killed and about 15 injured, and the Podilskyi and Darnytskyi bridges over the Dnipro were damaged along with a critical infrastructure site. Traffic between the two banks is badly disrupted and the mayor asked businesses to work remotely.

news.title: Ukraine says drones hit over 2 million targets this year
news.summary: Ukraine's Ministry of Defence says its forces struck more than 2 million targets with drones in 2026, all logged in the DELTA system and verified by Brave1. October was the busiest month with over 257,000 verified strikes, almost 2.5 times January. Targets include air defence, EW systems, drones, vehicles, boats and ground robots.

news.title: Quantum Systems' Ukraine joint venture to grow drone output fivefold
news.summary: Quantum Frontline Industries, a joint venture of Quantum Systems and Frontline Robotics, plans to raise drone production capacity fivefold in 2027 after a larger follow-on order from Ukraine's National Guard. It builds Ukrainian-designed Linza and Zoom drones in Germany. The partners will also spend over EUR 10 m on training, support and maintenance in Ukraine.

news.title: Poland: all three objects were Kh-101 missiles made in late 2026
news.summary: Polish prosecutors say debris at all three crash sites from 20 November came from Russian Kh-101 cruise missiles, not two missiles and a jet Shahed as first reported. The missiles were made in the fourth quarter of 2026 in Dubna, near Moscow. Poland is calling for stronger NATO air defences.

news.title: Drones reported over Russia's Baltic Fleet base in Kaliningrad
news.summary: Residents of Baltiysk reported explosions and air defence fire on the evening of 21 November, and OSINT analysts geolocated air defence firing from the port. Local authorities first said a suspicious object came from the direction of Lithuania. No hits are confirmed. A NATO E-3A surveillance aircraft monitored the area.

news.title: Dutch startup Hope Industries builds jet interceptor for a ministry challenge
news.summary: Hope Industries makes the electric Patronus E and is building the jet-powered Patronus H in response to a Dutch defence ministry challenge. The target is Shahed-type drones flying about 600 km/h at 5 km altitude within a 30 km radius. Work began three months ago, showing how fast challenge-based buying can move.

news.title: Canada joins the NATO Innovation Fund
news.summary: Canada has committed EUR 64.59 m (about CAD 100 m) to the NATO Innovation Fund and becomes its 25th participating nation. Total backing is now more than EUR 1.1 bn. Canada's development bank BDC will manage the stake.

news.title: Two Russian Kh-101 missiles and a jet Shahed crash in Poland
news.summary: Poland's defence minister confirmed that two Kh-101 cruise missiles came down at Nowy Lipowiec and Rudnik nad Sanem, and a jet-powered Shahed at Mołodycz, during Russia's attack on Ukraine on 20 November. Eleven aerial objects threatened Polish airspace, and he called it a deliberate provocation. Swedish Gripens were in the air but the pilot could not identify the missile to shoot it down. Investigators later concluded all three objects were Kh-101 missiles.

news.title: Netherlands starts WARDEN low-cost interceptor missile programme
news.summary: The Dutch defence ministry and Guardian Dynamics signed an MoU to develop WARDEN, a modular family of interceptor missiles priced at about EUR 30,000–75,000 each. Partners include Demcon, TNO and Aalberts, and the first phase starts in Q1 2027. The focus is the missile itself, to be integrated into existing air defence systems.

news.title: NATO launches STARLIFT for fast military satellite launches
news.summary: NATO unveiled STARLIFT at NATO Edge 26 in Izmir. Ten allies, including Norway, Sweden and Finland, plus South Korea fund it through NSPA. It reserves slots with commercial launch providers and uses a network of spaceports, and will test urgent launches of military satellites. Sweden says Esrange in Kiruna will play a key role.

news.title: EU ministers back eight joint capability areas, including a defence cloud
news.summary: EU defence ministers approved the 2026 Coordinated Annual Review on Defence and endorsed eight cooperation areas, including cruise missiles, space-based early warning, strategic air transport and a secure federated defence cloud. The European Defence Agency gets EUR 78 m for 2027, 8.7% more than this year.

press.titleNo: FMA gjennomfører nasjonal konkurranse om bygging av standardiserte fartøy
press.title: FMA runs a national competition to build the standardised vessels
press.summary: FMA says interest in the standardised vessels is high and it will run a national competition among Norwegian suppliers. The buy is split into two contracts and financial security requirements are reduced, so more yards can compete. Key figures such as equity are not absolute minimums, and yards can meet them through joint bids or a supporting company. Hulls may be built in Norway, but there is no general requirement for it. Prequalification is now under way.
press.startup: Two contracts and joint bids mean more yards in play, and each will need subsuppliers for sensors, autonomy and onboard systems. Talk to the yards that prequalify now (inference).
press.tldr: Navy ship race stays Norwegian; pitch onboard tech to the bidding yards.

press.titleNo: USA hentet norsk KI-hjelp til øvelse i Stillehavet
press.title: US brought in Norwegian AI help for a Pacific exercise
press.summary: A team from Cyberforsvaret and NOBLE, the battle lab at the Joint Headquarters, took a Norwegian AI tool to the PAX-SIX intelligence-sharing activity in Hawaii in October. The US organisers had seen it at Bold Quest in September. The tool combines language models, databases and dedicated hardware so it runs on closed networks. It translated Japanese and English, explained logs and error messages and helped make databases exchange ISR data. Kongsberg Defence staff were part of the team.
press.startup: Forsvaret builds and fields its own AI on closed networks with NOBLE. Startups with secure, offline AI tools should seek NOBLE as a test partner (inference).
press.tldr: Offline AI on closed networks works; NOBLE is the door in.

press.title: Government to invest in air defence missiles
press.summary: The revised 2026 defence budget proposes buying air defence missiles for about NOK 22 bn, with a P85 cost frame of NOK 21,257 m. The missiles are AIM-9X, AMRAAM 120C and AMRAAM Extended Range, all for NASAMS ground launchers. They will protect Ørland, Evenes, critical infrastructure, allied reception areas and Army forces against drones, aircraft and helicopters. The aim is to replace old missiles, replace those donated to Ukraine and build larger stocks. The minister says stocks also deter.
press.startup: The money goes to US missiles and Kongsberg, not to startups. The opening is around it: sensors, C2, cheap effectors and drone detection that let costly missiles be saved for the right targets (inference).
press.tldr: Big missile money goes to primes; sell what makes each missile count.

press.titleNo: Hæren kan ikke vinne kampen alene
press.title: The Army cannot win the fight alone
press.summary: On 17 November more than 150 people from Forsvaret, municipalities, business and emergency services met in Elverum to discuss the Army's endurance in war. The Chief of the Army said Forsvaret loses fighting power if it must spend resources keeping society running. Business leaders asked the Army to involve industry earlier in its planning, since much of the capacity it needs sits in private firms. One transport CEO said the next step is to move from goodwill to concrete agreements.
press.startup: The Army is opening up to firm agreements with private suppliers for wartime support. Logistics, communications and resilience startups should get into these planning talks early (inference).
press.tldr: Total defence is shifting to contracts; get into the Army's planning early.

press.title: Atlantic Future Forum 2026: co-hosts' statement
press.summary: Representatives of 29 countries met in Oslo on 11–12 November aboard HMS Prince of Wales, at the invitation of the UK and Norway. They affirmed NATO as the base of collective security and welcomed greater European leadership in deterrence and defence. They noted the Northern Navies Framework signed by Joint Expeditionary Force naval chiefs on 10 November. The statement backs continued support for Ukraine and whole-of-society resilience. It calls for more production, faster technological innovation and a stronger European defence industrial base, including start-ups and SMEs alongside established primes.
press.startup: A political signal, not a programme: no money or procurement is attached. It gives startups a quotable line when they ask Norwegian and British buyers for a place next to the primes (inference).
press.tldr: Norway and the UK say start-ups belong next to the primes; hold them to it.

press.title: The industry portal for Ukraine has changed
press.summary: The portal, set up in November 2024 for Norwegian offers of technology and materiel to Ukraine, is now a marketplace showing defence capacities and opportunities. Ukraine's defence ministry should as a rule verify that a product matches a Ukrainian need. The portal no longer gets annual earmarked Nansen funds; unused money moves to the ordinary military support budget. FMA assesses the commercial, technical and legal side of proposals that match confirmed needs, and Forsvaret decides based on Ukrainian priorities and the budget. A ministry review found the old setup lacked clear rules for handling cases.
press.startup: Registering an offer no longer means a funded project; buys happen only when Ukraine confirms a concrete need. Startups should register and also build direct contact with Ukrainian units and Brave1 to get needs confirmed (inference).
press.tldr: Register on the portal, but get Ukraine to confirm the need first.

press.title: Work begins on a Nordic defence agreement
press.summary: Norway, Denmark, Finland, Sweden and Iceland will start work on a Nordic defence agreement, agreed at the NORDEFCO ministers' meeting in Oslo on 11–12 November. The goal is closer cooperation that strengthens NATO deterrence and lets Nordic forces operate seamlessly across borders. Ministers discussed a legal and political framework for peace, crisis and war, and want to remove practical and legal obstacles to moving forces. The Nordic countries together have about 250 modern fighter jets, 145 surface vessels and 100,000 personnel in peacetime. No timeline was given.
press.startup: The release does not mention procurement, but common rules for moving forces point toward more shared exercises, logistics and systems (inference). Products that work across all Nordic forces will have a bigger market.
press.tldr: Nordic forces are integrating; sell to all five, not one.

press.title: MoD asks agencies to prepare corrective actions after audit
press.summary: Riksrevisjonen found that the 2025 accounts of Forsvaret, FFI and FMA may contain material errors, and could not give an opinion on Forsvarsbygg. The MoD has ordered concrete action plans with reporting requirements. Forsvaret must strengthen inventory control with an annual stock-count plan, FMA risks booking purchases in the wrong fiscal year, and Forsvarsbygg gets an external review of its financial management.
press.startup: Expect stricter documentation on deliveries, invoice timing and inventory traceability when you sell to FMA or Forsvaret. There may be demand for inventory, traceability and financial-control tools.
press.tldr: Expect stricter paperwork when you deliver to FMA and Forsvaret.

press.title: Forsvaret modernises its emergency-network radios
press.summary: Forsvaret will buy 1,320 new terminals for Nødnett, the radio network shared with police, fire and health services. About 650 replace first-generation equipment; the Army gets 280 and the Home Guard 290. The new handheld Motorola MXP600 replaces the MT P850S, delivered through TC Connect and funded through the Defence Staff's ICT portfolio. Forsvaret says it needs several ways to communicate, including robust ground systems alongside satellite and broadband, and that the upgrade also eases cooperation with Nordic emergency services.
press.startup: The contract is already placed, so there is nothing to bid on. It shows Forsvaret values redundant communications and civil-military interoperability in total defence, a theme comms and C2 startups can pitch to (inference).
press.tldr: No tender, but Forsvaret wants redundant comms that work with civilian services.

press.titleNo: Forsvarsmateriell inviterer norske verft til konkurranse om nye fartøy til Sjøforsvaret
press.title: Norwegian yards invited to compete for new Navy vessels
press.summary: National prequalification for up to 28 standardized vessels for the Navy, Coast Guard and allies: up to 10 ocean-going and 18 coastal. Split into two contracts to widen Norwegian participation. Vessels must be built in Norway; hulls may be built abroad. Apply via Mercell (documents, timeline, deadline); the notice is also on Doffin. Only a limited number of qualified suppliers will be invited to bid. Contact: forsvarsmateriell@fma.no, +47 23 09 30 03.
press.startup: Startups will not build ships, but autonomy, sensors, C2 software, drone hangars and maintenance tech can ride along as subsuppliers. Talk to the yards that prequalify.
press.tldr: Big ship deal: get in as a subsupplier through the yards.

press.titleNo: Regjeringen styrker norske investeringer i Ukraina med 1 milliard kroner
press.title: NOK 1 bn to strengthen Norwegian investment in Ukraine
press.summary: A NOK 1 bn framework over three years, taken from the military part of the Nansen programme and placed under the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries. Investinor manages it by investing in Norwegian-based funds that back Ukrainian defence companies. Investinor picks the funds; the fund managers pick the companies. Direct co-investments may follow.
press.startup: Norwegian–Ukrainian joint ventures and Ukrainian partners of Norwegian startups may become investable through these funds. Talk to Investinor and Norwegian defence-tech fund managers early.
press.tldr: New NOK 1 bn fund route makes Norwegian–Ukrainian ventures easier to finance.

press.titleNo: Styrker evnen til å oppdage droner i Finnmark
press.title: Stronger drone detection in Finnmark
press.summary: The Armed Forces place air-surveillance sensors (NASAMS) in Kirkenes to detect and warn of drones in the border area. About 30 soldiers from the Garrison of Sør-Varanger will be stationed there through the year. The deployment is preventive. Police enforce drone rules and the Armed Forces assist on request.
press.startup: Clear demand signal for low-cost drone detection and early warning in Arctic conditions. No tender is attached, but this is a use case to pitch to the Home Guard, FFI and FMA.
press.tldr: Clear demand for cheap Arctic drone detection, but no tender yet.

readings.title: The “Battle of Norway”
readings.publisher: Sahaidachnyi Security Center, supported by Buntar Aerospace
readings.summary: Argues that the most likely attack on Norway is not a ground invasion of Finnmark but a 'Battle of Britain' in the drone era: mass drone and missile strikes, sea drones and sabotage against energy, subsea cables and logistics. It sees a threat window of 2027–2029, while most Norwegian programmes mature in 2029–2036. Biggest gaps: counter-drone and ballistic defence, sabotage detection at sea, tactical electronic warfare and manpower in Finnmark. Recommends a standing Ukraine–Norway capability partnership, starting with a Home Guard counter-drone shield.
readings.tldr: Norway's real gap is cheap mass defence against drones and sabotage, and Ukraine can help close it fast.

readings.title: Sabotage threat in Norway raised
readings.summary: PST's updated assessment says Russian intelligence will likely attempt sabotage in Norway in the coming year, mostly through proxies. The defence industry, defence-related businesses and their suppliers are the most likely targets, followed by critical infrastructure such as energy. PST asks companies to know their normal picture and report anything that deviates from it.
readings.tldr: Defence startups and their suppliers are now named sabotage targets; secure your sites.

readings.title: EU strategy for a rapidly changing Arctic
readings.summary: The EU's new Arctic strategy replaces the 2021 framework and puts security and resilience first. It plans a maritime security hub for sharing information and monitoring Arctic waters, more icebreaker capacity and protection of critical infrastructure such as a secure subsea cable to Greenland. Russia's military build-up and hybrid tactics in the north are the stated reason.
readings.tldr: EU money and attention are moving to Arctic surveillance and infrastructure protection.

readings.title: National Threat Assessment 2026
readings.summary: Russian and Chinese intelligence activity is expected to rise, with focus on military targets, Ukraine support, the High North and critical infrastructure. Essential context for anyone selling security or surveillance tech.
readings.tldr: Russian and Chinese spying in Norway is rising; expect stricter security demands on suppliers.

readings.title: Fokus 2026
readings.summary: The intelligence service's annual open assessment of the external threats to Norway, with Russia's military posture in the north at the centre.
readings.tldr: Russia's military power in the north remains the core threat to Norway.

readings.title: Defence Expenditure of NATO Countries (2014–2026)
readings.summary: Official spending, share of GDP, equipment share and personnel for all allies. The numbers on the map above come from here.
readings.tldr: Every ally but Slovenia now spends 2%+ of GDP; the money is there.

readings.title: Forsvarsløftet: long-term plan for the defence sector 2025–2036
readings.summary: The cross-party plan behind about NOK 600 bn in extra defence spending over 12 years. Tells you what Norway will buy and when.
readings.tldr: NOK 600 bn extra over 12 years: this is Norway's shopping list.

readings.title: Meld. St. 33 (2024–2025): status of the long-term plan
readings.summary: Progress, challenges and risks in delivering the long-term plan. Useful to see where programmes are late and where faster solutions are needed.
readings.tldr: Several programmes are late; that is where faster solutions are welcome.

readings.title: Roadmap for increased production capacity in the defence industry
readings.summary: The government's roadmap for scaling Norwegian defence production. Relevant for manufacturers and suppliers to the primes.
readings.tldr: Norway wants more production at home; manufacturers and subsuppliers benefit.

readings.title: New law on defence and security procurement (report)
readings.summary: Proposal for a new procurement law for defence and security. Shapes how startups can be bought from in the future.
readings.tldr: Procurement rules are being rewritten; watch how they treat small firms.

readings.title: National Security Strategy
readings.summary: Norway's first national security strategy, tying together defence, total defence, economy and technology.
readings.tldr: Security now spans defence, economy and technology, which widens the dual-use market.

readings.title: Readiness Roadmap 2030
readings.summary: The EU's four flagships, including the European Drone Defence Initiative and Eastern Flank Watch, with milestones to 2030.
readings.tldr: The EU wants a working drone shield and eastern flank watch by 2027–2030.

readings.title: White Paper for European Defence – Readiness 2030
readings.summary: The ReArm Europe plan, up to EUR 800 bn, and the SAFE loan instrument. Explains where EU defence money flows.
readings.tldr: Up to EUR 800 bn in EU defence money; SAFE loans favour European suppliers.

readings.title: Defence spending: who is doing what? (July 2026)
readings.summary: Country-by-country analysis of NATO's 2026 figures and the path to the Hague 3.5% + 1.5% target.
readings.tldr: Spending is rising everywhere, fastest on the eastern flank and in the Nordics.

readings.title: Russia's hybrid warfare campaign in Europe
readings.summary: Briefing on sabotage, cyberattacks, disinformation and drone incursions across Europe.
readings.tldr: Sabotage and drone incursions are the new normal, creating demand for protection of critical infrastructure.

readings.title: Ukraine Support Tracker
readings.summary: Tracks military, financial and humanitarian aid to Ukraine by country.
readings.tldr: Shows who funds Ukraine and how much, so you can see where the money is.

calendar.title: EUDIS Defence Hackathon Norway
calendar.org: Kjeller Innovasjon and Startuplab (EU Defence Innovation Scheme)
calendar.tldr: EU-funded hackathon for defence builders and startups in Norway.

calendar.title: Oslo DefSec Industry Forum
calendar.tldr: Norway's defence-innovation debate in one morning. Our notes are below.

calendar.title: Open Arms Fest 2026
calendar.org: Ukrainian defence-tech platform (touring Oslo, Stockholm, Helsinki, Tallinn)
calendar.tldr: Ukrainian defence-tech companies met Norwegian government and business in Oslo.

calendar.title: Nordic Defense Summit 2026
calendar.tldr: Matchmaking and a live field demo with Nordic startups and Ukraine's Iron Cluster.

calendar.title: Nordic defence ministers' meeting
calendar.tldr: Closed meeting; watch the 12 November press briefing for Nordic joint buying and total defence news.

calendar.title: ReBuild Ukraine 2026 with Team Norway
calendar.tldr: Norwegian pavilion and a side event on financing Norwegian–Ukrainian business (11 Nov, 18:00). NUCC is in our network.

calendar.title: Slush 2026
calendar.tldr: Last day today: Europe's biggest startup event, with growing dual-use and defence tracks.

calendar.title: NEDS 2026 (NIDV Exhibition Defence & Security)
calendar.tldr: Expo day today; KNDS shows its FENNEK AIR counter-drone vehicle. A door into the Dutch MoD.

calendar.title: DroneDefenseHackathon26 Nordic
calendar.tldr: Counter-drone hackathon open to startups. Good for finding C-UAS talent and partners.

calendar.tldr: How to commercialise cold-weather innovation for defence. Directly relevant to Arctic use cases.

calendar.title: Dark Drones
calendar.tldr: Operating and detecting drones in cold, dark Norwegian waters, with an outdoor demo. Mainly for cluster members and invitees.

calendar.title: Oslo Security Conference 2027
calendar.tldr: Norway's main security-policy conference, usually in the first half of February. Dates not yet announced.

calendar.title: SecD-Day Conference & Exhibition
calendar.tldr: Finland's defence and security tech show. The Finnish MoD is easier to approach than most.

calendar.title: Munich Security Conference
calendar.tldr: Where Europe's defence agenda for the year gets set. Side events matter more than the main stage for startups.

calendar.title: AI in Defence Summit
calendar.tldr: One day on defence AI with founders, investors and EU officials.

calendar.title: Enforce Tac 2027
calendar.tldr: Germany's fair for internal and external security. Fast-growing defence and drone halls.

calendar.title: DSEI Germany
calendar.tldr: New German edition of DSEI. A route into the Bundeswehr supply chain.

calendar.title: NORDSEC Defence Hackathon 2027
calendar.org: NORDSEC (Nordic Defence and Security Cluster) and NTNU

funding.title: Innovative public procurement (Innovative offentlige anskaffelser)

funding.title: Industrial PhD (Nærings-ph.d.)
funding.amount: NOK 145.8 m in total; 36–48 month projects

funding.title: SkatteFUNN R&D tax deduction

funding.tldr: Easiest non-dilutive money in Norway. Apply early; 1 September guarantees a same-year decision.

funding.title: Defence and security technology in the USA
funding.who: Norwegian defence and security tech companies

funding.title: NATO Innovation Fund
funding.tldr: A EUR 1 bn NATO-backed VC fund. Pitch any time.

funding.title: EDF application advice
funding.who: Norwegian companies preparing EU defence bids
funding.tldr: Free help to get ready for the 2027 EDF calls. Start now; consortia take months.

funding.title: PES: support to build EU and EDF applications
funding.amount: Up to NOK 500k per application (depends on role)
funding.who: Norwegian actors with a formal role in an EU or EDF application
funding.tldr: Get paid to write your EDF bid. Apply at least four weeks before the EU deadline.

funding.title: Centres for defence capability, security and preparedness
funding.amount: Up to NOK 450 m for 5–9 centres
funding.who: Only applicants who sent a sketch by 5 June 2026
funding.tldr: Main call deadline is planned for 20 January 2027. Only sketch applicants can lead; join a consortium now.

funding.title: NOK 1 bn Ukraine defence investment scheme
funding.amount: Fund investments, NOK 1 bn over 3 years

funding.tldr: Proposed November 2026. Norwegian–Ukrainian ventures should talk to fund managers now.

funding.title: Brave Norway

funding.tldr: The Norway–Ukraine startup programme. Watch FFI and Brave1 for the next call.

funding.title: NATO DIANA challenge programme
funding.tldr: 2027 call closed 3 July 2026. Prepare now for the next call, usually mid-year.

funding.title: European Defence Fund (EDF) 2026 calls
funding.who: EU and EEA companies, Norway included
funding.tldr: 2026 calls closed 29 September. The 2027 work programme comes next.

funding.title: LINC: Launchpad for Innovative Norwegian Companies
funding.tldr: 2026 intake closed 20 April. Expect the next round in spring 2027.

tenders.title: P1118 standardized vessels: prequalification

tenders.title: Digital learning platform for the defence sector (incl. AI content)

tenders.title: Laboratory services for the Norwegian defence
tenders.tldr: Re-announced with a new deadline. Relevant for testing and lab companies.

tenders.title: Operation of Forsvaret's unclassified internet services
tenders.tldr: Hosting and operations incl. Azure. For IT and cloud operators.

tenders.title: Dynamic purchasing system: software licences

tenders.title: Visitor registration system for Forsvarsbygg
